identity.name: Principality of Theodoro
alt_names: Lordship of Theodoro and the Maritime Region

land.text: Mangup and the principality, which surrendered to the Ottomans at the end of December 1475

successors.note: 'With the fall of Mangup, the principality ceased to exist'; the coast was taken in the same campaign (Caffa fell by 6 June 1475). Cliopatria's row ends in 1474.

capitals.name: Mangup (Doros, Theodoro)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Mangup (Doros, Theodoro)'. The capital 'Doros, also sometimes called Theodoro and now known as Mangup'. The page gives no years; Tamerlane destroyed 'Gothia's capital Theodoro' in 1395.

rulers.name: Demetrios
rulers.note: 'c.1362-c.1368, first recorded' (infobox); the name Theodoro appears in a Greek inscription c. 1361/1362.

rulers.name: Alexios I
rulers.note: Ascended 'c.1410/1411 at the latest', reportedly with Genoese help; died 1444-45 or 1447. His son John's reign 'may have been very short or nonexistent'. The page's list has gaps (c. 1368-c. 1410).

rulers.name: Olubei
rulers.note: 'succeeded as prince in c. 1447 and ruled until c. 1458'.

rulers.name: Isaac
rulers.note: 'In 1465, Prince Isaac is mentioned'; overthrown in 1475 by his brother Alexander for his pro-Ottoman stance. Start of his reign not on the page.

rulers.name: Alexander
rulers.note: Last prince; backed by his brother-in-law Stephen the Great of Moldavia.

keyframe_review.note: 1,331 km2 (four grid cells from the Inkerman area to east of Mangup). The page gives no area, no boundary and no founding year: it says only that the principality 'is first mentioned in the early 14th century' (a 'Prince of Gothia' under Andronikos III, 1328-1341, so Cliopatria's 1333 is plausible), that the capital is Mangup in the Crimean Mountains and that Greek inscriptions are found at Inkerman. Shape kept; the halving of the area in 1375 is not explained by the page (see _1375).

Years only: 653.5 km2 holds 1375-1422. Cliopatria halves the area in 1375 (1,331 to 653.5 km2), but the page records no loss in the 14th century: it dates only the Mongol tribute from 1238, the Blue Waters battle c. 1362/63 and Tamerlane's destruction of the capital in 1395. Kept as the inland core; the cause may be Cliopatria's Genoa row (Genoese Gazaria page: 'Capitanatu Gotia (territory of Theodoro)'). The Gothia page tried after review is a disambiguation page with no dated mention of 1333, 1375 or a loss to Genoa; the halving stays unexplained.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1423-1432: 'From the first half of the 15th century it also included parts of the coastline, now stretching from Kalamita Bay in the west to possibly as far east as modern Rybache just west of Kanaka'; Prince Alexios 'began to challenge the Genoese for control over the Genoese province of Gothia' (the coast from Cembalo to Lusta) and in 1423 attacked them; 'by the 1420s the official titulature of the prince read Lord of the city of Theodoro and the Maritime Region'; Cembalo (Balaklava) is subtracted: the page has it Genoese until the Greek rising of February 1433 (next keyframe). Cliopatria keeps the inland core of 653.5 km2 to 1474 and has no coast. Two 20 km discs at Sevastopol and Yalta stand for the strip; they are the researcher's reading, the page gives no boundary (confidence low). Fixed after review: the first version drew Cembalo as Theodoro's for the whole 1423-1475 span although it was Genoese before 1433 and after June 1434. On the project's grid Balaklava has no land cell of its own and the 15 km Cembalo disc reaches the Inkerman and Mangup cells (Theodoro's core), so Cembalo is subtracted from the coastal discs only, never from the Cliopatria core; the drawn cells do not change.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1433: 'Alexios supported a Greek rebellion in Cembalo in February 1433' and 'A Genoese force reconquered Cembalo in June 1434'; the page says 'While Alexios lost Cembalo it seems that he retained the rest of his conquests', so Cembalo counts as Theodoro's from February 1433 (confidence 2: the page says 'supported a rebellion', not that the town passed to him) until June 1434. The episode is 16 months long and one town; it is a one-year keyframe, and the year 1434, in which the town is lost in June, takes the shape of the next keyframe. The page does not say who held Cembalo after its second revolt of 1439.

Cliopatria ends the row in 1474 but the page ends the principality at the surrender of Mangup 'at the end of December 1475'; the years 1468-1475 are covered by principality-of-theodoro_1434 (the coast without Cembalo, which the page has Genoese from June 1434). ledger.note: 1333: the Principality of Gothia/Theodoro in the Crimean mountains (a bridging date). The page does not date a founding: it says the principality 'is first mentioned in the early 14th century', citing a 'Prince of Gothia' under Andronikos III (1328-1341), and that the name Theodoro first appears in an inscription of c. 1361/1362; 1333 is Cliopatria's first year, inside that reign. The Mongols had 'enforced a tribute on the western half, including Gothia' in 1238. Pages tried after review: the Mangup page dates the rise of the principality to 'the late 13th/early 14th century' when 'Mangup became the centre of the Principality of Theodoro' (no year), and the Gothia disambiguation page says 'Greek principality in southern Crimea from early 14th century to 1475'; neither gives a year, so 1333 stays Cliopatria's bridging year at confidence 1.

ledger.note: 1423: Prince Alexios holds a coastal strip taken from the Genoese province of Gothia. 'From the first half of the 15th century it also included parts of the coastline'; Alexios 'began to challenge the Genoese for control over the Genoese province of Gothia' from c. 1410/1411; 'In 1423 prince Alexios attacked and the Genoese had to spend a large sum of money to repel him'; 'by the 1420s' he is 'Lord of ... the Maritime Region'. The page dates no capture: 1423, the first dated attack, bridges the silence; the extent is a reading of 'Kalamita Bay in the west to possibly ... Rybache'. Cembalo (Balaklava) is subtracted: the page has it Genoese until the rising of February 1433 and again from June 1434, so it is drawn as Theodoro's only for those months (events of 1433 and 1434).

February 1433: Theodoro backs a Greek rising at Cembalo. 'February 1433: Alexios supported a Greek rebellion in Cembalo' (the Genoese port, Balaklava), the first dated fighting over the coast since the 1423 attack.

February 1433: Cembalo (Balaklava) passes to the Greek rebels backed by Theodoro. 'Alexios supported a Greek rebellion in Cembalo in February 1433'; the page then says 'A Genoese force reconquered Cembalo in June 1434' and 'While Alexios lost Cembalo it seems that he retained the rest of his conquests', so the town counts as Theodoro's for those sixteen months (confidence 2: the year and the month are the page's, that the town passed to Theodoro is the researcher's reading of 'lost Cembalo'). The loss of June 1434 undoes this gain. The Alexios I of Theodoro page, which might date the capture, would not load.

June 1434: Genoa recovers Cembalo. 'A Genoese force reconquered Cembalo in June 1434 and plundered Kalamita, which had been abandoned'; Kalamita was reclaimed by Theodoro and Cembalo revolted again in 1439 (page).

June 1434: Cembalo is lost to Genoa. 'While Alexios lost Cembalo it seems that he retained the rest of his conquests.' The page does not date Theodoro's earlier hold of Cembalo beyond the 1433 rising.

1475: Alexander overthrows Isaac. Isaac's 'increasingly pro-Ottoman stance ... led to his overthrow by his brother Alexander in 1475', backed by Stephen the Great of Moldavia; on 20 June 1475 the prince wrote to the Hungarian king that Theodoro had been 'captured by Alexander'. Same state, new prince.

wars.name: Tamerlane's raid on Gothia
wars.outcome: Tamerlane destroyed several towns including Gothia's capital Theodoro; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Theodoro-Genoese conflicts over Gothia
wars.outcome: 1423: Alexios attacks and the Genoese pay a large sum to repel him; February 1433 Theodoro backs a rising at Cembalo; June 1434 Genoa retakes Cembalo and plunders Kalamita, which Theodoro reclaims; Cembalo revolts again in 1439. Theodoro keeps the rest of its coastal conquests.
wars.note: The page says the principality 'was in constant strife with Genoese Gazaria colonies to the south over access to the coasts'.

wars.outcome: The Ottoman fleet leaves Constantinople on 20 May 1475, takes Caffa by 6 June, besieges Theodoro castle from September; Mangup surrenders at the end of December 1475 and the principality ends.
wars.note: The Crimean Khanate allied with the sultan in 1475 and became an Ottoman vassal; much of the rest of Crimea remained Khanate land.

certainty.note: Crimean mountain principality: the page names places (Mangup, Inkerman, Kalamita, Cembalo, Rybache) but no boundary or treaty line; the coastal strip of 1423-1475 is a reading.

notes: Written 2026-10-19 by eu-05-e from two pages (budget 1-2); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captainship_of_Gothia would not load (url_not_found twice), so the Genoese side (when the Captainship of Gothia was formed, which coast it covered) rests on the Theodoro page. Dates: the page gives no founding year, so start 1333 is Cliopatria's (confidence 1); the end is December 1475 (Cliopatria 1474; Genoese Gazaria text says 1474, its infobox and the Theodoro page 1475). Cliopatria's shapes: 1333 (1,331 km2) kept; the 1375 halving (to 653.5 km2) and the absence of any coast are not explained by the page, which says the principality held 'parts of the coastline' from the first half of the 15th century; 1423-1475 is a new keyframe adding two 20 km discs (Sevastopol, Yalta) for the 'Maritime Region'. The Genoa dossier (eu-13) draws the Captainship of Gothia (Cembalo to Lusta) over the same coast in Cliopatria, so its owner should subtract the strip. No area on the page, so no area comparison. Overlordships for other dossiers: tribute as vassals to the Golden Horde (no years), the Mongol tribute from 1238 on the western half of Crimea including Gothia; the Crimean Khanate (from 1450 in Cliopatria) and the Ottomans after 1475; the page mentions no tribute to Trebizond ('Gazarian Perateia ... a weak dependence after 1204'). Not settled: the founding year; the date of Alexios's conquests; Kalamita's holder 1434-1439; the list of princes between c. 1368 and c. 1410 and the reign of Isaac; whether Avlita and Funa belonged to Theodoro (not on the page). The Genoese Gazaria page spells the Cembalo coast only as 'Capitanatu Gotia'. Review fixes 2026-10-19: Cembalo (Balaklava) subtracted from the 1423 coastal strip (it was Genoese before February 1433 and after June 1434); a gain of Cembalo from republic-of-genoa added for February 1433 (confidence 2) so that the June 1434 loss undoes it; the 1423-1475 keyframe is split into 1423-1432 (without Cembalo), 1433 (with Cembalo) and 1434-1475 (without), and the 1468 verdict, the 1475 loss and the dissolve use the strip without Cembalo. Grid caveat: Balaklava has no land cell of its own on the project grid (its cell is sea) and the 15 km Cembalo disc of the 1433/1434 events reaches the Inkerman and Mangup cells, so those events resolve to Theodoro's own core cells; the subtraction is applied to the coastal discs only. The Alexios I of Theodoro page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexios_I_of_Theodoro, also tried as Alexios_of_Theodoro) would not load (url_not_found), so the date of the capture of the coastal strip stays unsettled. Founding year: the Mangup and Gothia pages give only 'late 13th/early 14th century' and 'early 14th century'.
